rows.sentence: Based on the document, here is what the document says:
rows.label: no_rad
rows.rationale: This introduces the answer without making a substantive factual claim.

rows.sentence: Mpox (formerly known as monkeypox) is a disease caused by infection with a virus, known as Monkeypox virus.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The context explicitly gives the disease's former name and identifies its cause.

rows.sentence: This virus is part of the same family as the virus that causes smallpox.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The context explicitly places the two viruses in the same family.

rows.sentence: Mpox is a zoonotic disease, meaning it can be spread between animals and people.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The context states that mpox is zoonotic and explains what that means.

rows.sentence: It is endemic, or found regularly, in parts of Central and West Africa.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The context identifies parts of Central and West Africa as areas where mpox is endemic.

rows.sentence: The first human case of mpox was recorded in 1970, in what is now the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The context explicitly gives the year and location of the first recorded human case.

rows.sentence: The World Health Organization "renamed the disease in 2022," though "The virus that causes it still has its historic name."
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The context states that the WHO renamed the disease in 2022 and that the virus retained its historic name.

rows.sentence: Is it currently spreading?
rows.label: no_rad
rows.rationale: This section heading poses a question rather than asserting a fact.

rows.sentence: In 2022, mpox spread around the world.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The context explicitly reports worldwide spread in 2022.

rows.sentence: Clade I is responsible for the current rise of cases in Central and Eastern Africa.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The context explicitly attributes the current rise in those regions to clade I.

rows.sentence: Clade II is the type that caused the global outbreak that began in 2022.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The context explicitly identifies clade II as the cause of the global outbreak that started in 2022.

rows.sentence: The document does not state whether mpox is spreading outside these described situations beyond the "current rise of cases in Central and Eastern Africa."
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The document identifies a current rise in Central and Eastern Africa, dates the global spread to 2022, and describes endemic areas without specifying whether spread is currently occurring elsewhere.

rows.sentence: People with mpox often get a rash, along with other symptoms.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The context explicitly identifies a rash as a common symptom and mentions other symptoms.

rows.sentence: The rash will go through several stages, including scabs, before healing.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The context explicitly describes the rash progressing through stages, including scabs, before healing.

rows.sentence: Although cases of mpox are not life-threatening, some people may be more likely to get severely ill, including People with severely weakened immune systems, Children younger than 1, People with a history of eczema, People who are pregnant.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The risk section uses the same qualification and lists all four groups as more likely to get severely ill.

rows.sentence: Historically, clade I caused higher numbers of severe illnesses than clade II, with up to 10% of people dying from it.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The context explicitly makes the historical severity comparison and gives the same upper death-rate figure.

rows.sentence: Recent outbreaks have seen much lower death rates of about 1-3.3%.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The context gives this range for recent outbreaks in its discussion of clade I.

rows.sentence: Infections from clade II mpox are generally less severe.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The context explicitly describes clade II infections as generally less severe.

rows.sentence: More than 99.9% of people survive.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The context gives this survival figure for people with clade II mpox, the subject of the preceding sentence.

rows.sentence: There are several ways you can protect yourself and others from mpox:
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The context explicitly introduces several measures to protect oneself and others from mpox.

rows.sentence: Getting vaccinated.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The context lists vaccination as a prevention measure.

rows.sentence: Check with your healthcare provider to find out if the mpox vaccine is recommended for you.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The context explicitly recommends checking with a healthcare provider about eligibility for vaccination.

rows.sentence: Avoiding close, skin-to-skin contact with people who have a rash that looks like mpox.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The context lists this exact contact precaution as a prevention measure.

rows.sentence: Avoiding contact with materials that a person with mpox has used, including sharing eating utensils and cups, and handling their bedding or clothing.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The context recommends avoiding materials used by someone with mpox and gives the same examples.

rows.sentence: If you do get mpox, isolate at home, and cover lesions and wear a mask if you must be around others.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The context gives all three precautions and specifies when to cover lesions and wear a mask.

rows.sentence: If you are in an area of Western or Central Africa where mpox occurs regularly, avoid contact with live or dead wild animals.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The context gives the same advice and limits it to areas of Western or Central Africa where mpox occurs regularly.
